The sugarcane owner gave the piece of sugarcane by throwing it backward behind him without even looking at the child.

He gave it this way because he did not really want to give it (he was reluctant/unwilling)
An unwilling giver typically shows a scowling face and jerky, aggressive movements because their internal reluctance to give creates a visible conflict with the physical act of sharing.

If I’m giving something to someone, I should always have a big, sweet smile and use both hands to show I really respect them. I want to look them in the eye kindly so they feel happy and not shy or embarrassed. To me, giving should be done gladly and gently, making the other person feel like they are receiving a special gift from a friend

No, he could not. Even though he owned a vast forest of dark sugarcane as a Peta (hungry ghost), he was unable to eat any of it. Every time he tried to reach for a stalk to break it off, the sugarcane plants would sway away and hit him back.
This happened because of his bad karma. In his past life, he gave the sugarcane to the child unwillingly and threw it backward behind him. Because his act of giving lacked respect and genuine kindness, his reward was cursed so that he could not enjoy his own wealth.

If my friends are unable to access the fundamental needs such as food, medication, or stationery, they are likely to experience a lot of physical and psychological difficulties such as being weak due to a lack of food, poor performance at school due to a lacking education because of unavailability of stationery or because they are unable to attend school due to a lack of necessary gear such as a school bag or being sick due to a lack of medication. Such conditions are likely to make them very sad and anxious and even ashamed or lonely because they are unable to do the same things that everyone else is doing. As a friend, I can assist them by providing them with food and stationery that I can spare, donate clothing that I do not wear anymore, and the most important thing is to assist them with a goodhearted and polite expression so that they are not embarrassed.
an adult and a young child were following closely behind him.

When giving or donating to others, the most important thing is to have a pure and willing heart, which is referred to as “Cetanā." We have to be glad that we are able to help them, rather than feeling like it is an obligation or like we are parting with our own property. When we have a positive attitude like this, our physical gestures should reinforce this attitude. We should give our donations with both hands, with a warm smile on our face, with our eyes contacting the recipient’s kindly, with our position when giving or donating, standing or sitting low, so that the person we are giving to knows we respect them, so that the giving or donating process is a source of joy for the giver as well as for the receiver.

If children have to accept something from someone who is giving it unwillingly, they generally feel humiliated and saddened because they can sense the lack of kindness, which makes them feel like a burden rather than a person being cared for.

When I give or donate to others, I will do it respectfully, cheerfully, and with both hands. I will look the recipient in the eye with a warm smile to show that I am happy to share with them.
 I will give this way because, as we learned from the story of the sugarcane owner, the manner of giving is just as important as the gift itself. Giving with a willing heart and respect (Cetanā) brings happiness to both the giver and the receiver, and it ensures that the good deeds we do will bring us positive and peaceful results in the future.
